claims.text: Under the DoD Financial Management Regulation, a member on active duty is authorized a housing allowance based on grade, location and whether the member has dependents, and a housing allowance generally is not authorized for a member who is assigned to appropriate and adequate Government quarters.

A housing allowance generally is not authorized for a Service member who is assigned to appropriate and adequate Government quarters.' Par. 5.0 repeats that assignment to Government quarters affects BAH eligibility and that a housing allowance other than BAH-Partial or BAH-Diff is generally not authorized for a member assigned adequate quarters.
claims.scope: All uniformed services, United States locations, active duty entitled to basic pay
claims.locator: DoD 7000.14-R Vol 7A Ch 26 (May 2025), par. 2.0 Introduction (page 26-7) and par. 5.0 (page 26-25)

answerPassages.question: Will I live in the dorms or draw BAH as a student at NAS Pensacola or Corry Station?
answerPassages.answer: Navy Housing's NAS Pensacola page states that most personnel in E-1 through E-3, and E-4s with fewer than four years of service, are required to live in unaccompanied housing, and that E-4s may be required to live on base, space permitting. For an unaccompanied first-term student at Corry Station, the default is a dorm room and BAH-Partial. Your orders, your dependency status and the installation's occupancy decide your case, and only the UH office and your finance office can confirm it.
answerPassages.scope: Unaccompanied Navy students at NAS Pensacola and Corry Station; other services follow their own rule
answerPassages.caveat: Your orders, your dependency status and the installation's occupancy decide your case, and only the UH office and your finance office can confirm it.

answerPassages.question: Do Air Force CSO students at the 479th Flying Training Group live in the dorms?
answerPassages.answer: The 479th Flying Training Group welcome guide tells CSO students that if they are on unaccompanied orders they will be assigned to the Unaccompanied Officers Quarters on arrival regardless of rank or time in service, while students on accompanied orders may live on or off base and must contact the Housing office before signing a lease or closing on a house. That is command guidance dated 27 August 2026 for Undergraduate CSO Training only; it can change, and it does not describe Air Force enlisted students or the Navy dorms.
answerPassages.scope: Air Force undergraduate CSO students assigned to the 479 STUS at NAS Pensacola
answerPassages.caveat: That is command guidance dated 27 August 2026 for Undergraduate CSO Training only; it can change, and it does not describe Air Force enlisted students or the Navy dorms.

answerPassages.question: Is a Pensacola course a PCS or a TDY, and why does that change my housing?
answerPassages.answer: Under the Joint Travel Regulations, a course scheduled for 139 or fewer days (less than 20 weeks) is attended in a TDY status, and a course scheduled for 140 or more days (20 weeks) is a PCS with the course location as the permanent duty station. The status decides which quarters rule and which allowance apply. Read the order type on your actual orders, because the scheduled course length sets the status and the Secretary concerned can designate exceptions.
answerPassages.scope: Students on training orders to any Pensacola-area school
answerPassages.caveat: Read the order type on your actual orders, because the scheduled course length sets the status and the Secretary concerned can designate exceptions.

answerPassages.question: What is the 2026 BAH for an E-4 student at Corry Station?
answerPassages.answer: For 2026, the Pensacola military housing area (FL064, which covers NAS Pensacola, Corry Station and NAS Whiting Field) pays an E-4 without dependents $1,521 a month in BAH. The 2026 FL064 with-dependents BAH for an E-4 is $1,794 a month. Check the BAH line on your LES, because a published rate is not your entitlement and it is not a home-price limit.
